input.subject: Arabic translations
input.message:
Hello,

We don't have a translator in house. Can your team translate the remaining 340 strings for the new screens into Arabic? We need them by next Thursday.

Thanks
input.source: sample M05 (email from Faisal Al Mansoori, Operations Director, Gulf Freight Lines)

screen.label: Safety screen
screen.job: Strips hidden text and flags instructions aimed at the AI.

splitter.label: Request Splitter
splitter.job: Splits the client's message into atomic asks, quoting their words.

matcher.label: Scope Matcher
matcher.job: Classifies each ask against the signed SOW and cites the clauses.

check.label: Citation check
check.job: Every verdict must cite SOW clauses that exist and support it; else 'ambiguous'.

estimator.label: Change-Request Estimator
estimator.job: Estimates hours by role for out-of-scope asks from Empower's history.

pricing.label: CR pricing
pricing.job: Change-request price = hours x the SOW's rates + PM overhead.

reply.label: Reply Drafter
reply.job: Drafts the client reply: covered, change request with price, or a question.

guard.label: Leak guard
guard.job: Blocks internal costs, margins or prompt text in the client reply.

items.basis: A1 assigns Arabic translations to Gulf Freight Lines, while S1 includes Arabic localization for every screen. Estimate only the limited Empower effort to prepare/hand off the string file and check the supplied translations are usable; no new translation implementation is estimated because the Arabic screen support is already in scope. This is a small change relative to a full mobile module and consistent with the existing fleet-tracking system.
assumptions: Gulf Freight Lines supplies and approves all 340 Arabic translations as required by A1.
Professional translation and any third-party translation service costs are not included.
The existing screens and string-file format are unchanged; defects against agreed Arabic acceptance criteria remain subject to W1.
